answer: Agent economies can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to emit a unique, non-replayable signal tied to scarce real-world or computational resources that an attacker must provision separately. Creating many fakes multiplies costs because every identity needs its own persistent echo of verifiable activity that cannot be cheaply forged, and a supporting zephyr of continuous, low-latency proofs that detect parallelization or cloning. This raises the economic barrier to mass identity creation substantially.
